title: Shifting EXDATEs and Overrides by Wall-Clock Delta Across DST Under SHIFT_WITH_SERIES

citations.verbatim_quote: Note that since this is an entire rescheduling of the event, any instance-specific information will be lost, unless explicitly included with the update "REQUEST".
For a given pair of "UID" and "SEQUENCE" property values, the "RECURRENCE-ID" value for a recurrence instance is fixed.
Subsequent instances defined in separate components are not impacted by the given recurrence instance.

rationale: When a user shifts the start date or time of an entire recurring series (`recurrence_id=None`, changing `dtstart` without replacing `rrule` or changing `DATE` vs `DATE-TIME` value type or floating vs timezone-aware class), pruning exceptions (`PRUNE_INVALID` in R-L4-004 and R-L4-005) discards every single-instance deletion and override whenever the time of day changes. Under `series_reschedule_exception_mode = SHIFT_WITH_SERIES`, the store computes the wall-clock delta between the old and new master `DTSTART` (`naive(new_dtstart) - naive(old_dtstart)`) and shifts `EXDATE`, `RDATE`, inherited `RRULE.UNTIL`, and each standalone override's `RECURRENCE-ID` and `DTSTART` by that wall-clock delta (re-attaching the target timezone and preserving each override's duration). Using wall-clock delta rather than elapsed UTC duration is essential across DST transitions: moving `2025-03-08 09:00 EST` (`14:00Z`) to `2025-03-09 10:00 EDT` (`14:00Z`) is 24 hours in UTC (`+1d +0h`) yet `+1 day +1 hour` in local wall-clock time (`09:00 -> 10:00`). Because RFC 5545 Section 3.8.4.4 fixes `RECURRENCE-ID` per `(UID, SEQUENCE)`, re-keying a shifted override increments its `SEQUENCE` above both its own prior `SEQUENCE` and any `SEQUENCE` previously held at its new `(UID, RECURRENCE-ID)` key (satisfying invariant I-T-005).
store_implication: Under `series_reschedule_exception_mode = SHIFT_WITH_SERIES`, when a whole-series edit (`recurrence_id=None`, not normalized from a first-instance `THIS_AND_FUTURE` edit) changes `dtstart` without supplying a new `rrule` and without changing temporal class (`DATE`, floating `DATE-TIME`, or timezone-aware `DATE-TIME`): (1) compute `wall_delta = naive(new_dtstart) - naive(old_dtstart)`; (2) if `wall_delta != 0`, shift unpatched `exdate`, `rdate`, and any `UNTIL` bound in the inherited `rrule` on the main component by `wall_delta` in local wall-clock time; (3) shift each standalone override's `recurrence_id` and `dtstart` by `wall_delta` in local wall-clock time (preserving `TZID`/`Z` qualification on `recurrence_id` per I-K-004 and recomputing `dtend`/`due` to preserve the override's duration) and bump the override's `sequence`, `dtstamp`, and `last_modified`; and (4) prune any shifted `exdate` or override that still does not match a candidate occurrence of the updated main component.
edge_cases_and_counterexamples: DST spring-forward (`America/New_York` 2025-03-08 EST `-05:00` to 2025-03-09 EDT `-04:00`): shifting master `DTSTART` from `2025-03-08T09:00-05:00` to `2025-03-09T10:00-04:00` has a wall-clock delta of `+1 day, +1 hour` (even though the UTC delta is `+24 hours`). An `EXDATE` at `2025-03-09T09:00-04:00` shifts to `2025-03-10T10:00-04:00` (excluding the new 2nd occurrence), and an override at `RECURRENCE-ID TZID=America/New_York:20250310T090000` (`DTSTART 11:00-04:00`) shifts to `RECURRENCE-ID TZID=America/New_York:20250311T100000` (`DTSTART 12:00-04:00`).

When the whole-series edit also replaces `rrule` or transitions across temporal classes (`DATE <-> DATE-TIME` or `floating <-> UTC/TZID`), `SHIFT_WITH_SERIES` does not guess a mapping and falls back to pruning incompatible exceptions (R-L1-007).

scenarios.name: whole_series_dtstart_shift_across_dst_shifts_exdate_and_override_wall_clock
scenarios.description: Under series_reschedule_exception_mode=SHIFT_WITH_SERIES (and MASTER_ONLY), shifting an America/New_York daily series across the 2025-03-09 spring-forward DST boundary from 2025-03-08 09:00 EST to 2025-03-09 10:00 EDT shifts both EXDATE and the standalone override by the +1d +1h wall-clock delta and increments sequence on both components.

audit_notes: Added explicit rule and spring-forward DST scenario covering series_reschedule_exception_mode=SHIFT_WITH_SERIES.
Verified citations in rfc5546.txt Section 4.4.7 (L5862-L5864) and rfc5545.txt Section 3.8.4.4 (L6422-L6424, L6432-L6434).
